name: Ustekinumab
route_note: Subcutaneous injection every 12 weeks (psoriasis) or 8 weeks (IBD); single weight-based IV induction dose for IBD
owner: Johnson & Johnson (Janssen); biosimilars from several companies

discovery.note: Fully human IgG1κ antibody against the p40 subunit shared by IL-12 and IL-23.

tagline: IL-12/IL-23 p40 antibody for psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis and IBD
summary: Ustekinumab is a human monoclonal antibody against the p40 subunit shared by interleukins 12 and 23. Dosed every 8 to 12 weeks, it treats plaque psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis, Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis; biosimilars launched in the US and Europe from 2024–2025.
mechanism: IL-12 and IL-23 are heterodimeric cytokines sharing the p40 subunit. IL-12 drives Th1 differentiation and IFN-γ production; IL-23 sustains Th17 cells that produce IL-17 and IL-22.
Ustekinumab binds p40 and prevents both cytokines from engaging the IL-12Rβ1 receptor chain on T cells and NK cells, suppressing Th1 and Th17 inflammation in skin, joints and gut.
uses: Moderate to severe plaque psoriasis (adults and children)

history.title: First approval
history.detail: Approved in Canada in December for plaque psoriasis.

history.title: EU and US approval
history.detail: Approved in the EU in January and by the FDA in September.

history.title: Crohn's disease
history.detail: Approved for Crohn's disease with IV induction (UNITI).

history.title: First biosimilar
history.detail: FDA approves Wezlana (ustekinumab-auub), the first ustekinumab biosimilar, later designated interchangeable.

history.title: US biosimilar launches
history.detail: Multiple ustekinumab biosimilars launch in the US after patent settlements.

pk.metabolism: Proteolytic catabolism to peptides and amino acids (no CYP metabolism)
pk.excretion: Not renally excreted as intact antibody; cleared by catabolism and target-mediated uptake

facts: Ustekinumab was the first approved biologic targeting the IL-12/IL-23 pathway.
Maintenance dosing for psoriasis is only four times a year after loading.
